description: Settle an element that more than one machine has written: keep it or drop it with a stamp newer than anything in the log, so the decision wins on every node as the change propagates. Use it after read_conflicts named the element and you have decided how it should stand — re-creating it with the existing tools is not enough, because a write that already exists is skipped, and deleting what is already tombstoned changes nothing. An element that already stands as you ask is left untouched and reported as unchanged, because every write is durable history. An observation needs the entity to exist, and a relation both of its endpoints, exactly as when they were created.

elements.description: One entry per element: an observation or a relation, and whether it stands

content.description: The observation content; give it with entityName

entityName.description: The entity that holds an observation; give it with content

from.description: The name where a relation starts; give it with to and relationType

keep.description: True to make the element stand, false to make it go

relationType.description: The relation type; give it with from and to

to.description: The name where a relation ends; give it with from and relationType
